Shadowrun: Hong Kong Is $19 Well Spent

While not quite as good as Dragonfall: Director's Cut - Hong Kong certainly has it's moments where it shines brighter than previous entries. The revamped Matrix is a good addition to the game and keeps missions involving it interesting almost like a mini-game. The storyline itself is pretty good with plenty of grey areas that you come to love about the setting. There was some bugginess and to be honest, I didn't quite know how to play the Matrix areas for a while so there was some self inflicted anguish for a portion of the game but none of this really diminished my time playing the game.

In short - for $19, you get your money's worth and then some. It is easy to get immersed in this dark, fast and edgy setting. Hong Kong proves to be a perfect place to spent some time in the shadows.

I certainly agree. It's just not ProtectVoat's fault:

  • This community was already up and running before AskVoat was taken away from its community.

  • We had already told Atko and Puttitout exactly what the consequences of their 'letter, not spirit' interpretation of policy could be when awarding the huge AskVoat subverse to a user with no real history on the site.

  • We pleaded that Voat in alpha development should still be a place open to modification of obviously silly rules (and the rules were indeed modified not long after).

  • We protested heavily that the harsh words from admins and the implicit support for the small minority that wanted a censorship agenda were damaging to the community.

  • We asked Puttitout to come forward and explain; failing that we asked Atko to voice his opinion as the site's founder.

Admins again and again ignored every single appeal to sanity made from us. We won in the end, but it never had to include so many casualties.

That being said I'm more proud of how ProtectVoat manages to act as a watchdog in smaller and much less dramatic cases.

It's great when users bring a censorship issue to the community's attention, we discuss with the mods in question and everything is worked out to the benefit of everyone.

We shouldn't - and don't - seek confrontation for confrontation's sake. I'm just acutely aware that without us, trolls and SJWs would've killed this place a long time ago: Voat's only viable market position is that of a free speech community. There are a million other places to come for 'a safe space'.

The problem I see is relying on the admins. We can't count on them, they have lives and this path leads to abuse. They had already removed Askvoat from default, they shouldn't do more.

I know that without PV Voat would be dead, but I think that we could be much better.

And I agree, but remember it's a process. We were almost toppled by vicious trolling ourselves, but the community managed to push back and it seems like it has helped.

Voat is experiencing growing pains, as are we. Let's see if the host itself wants to live on or quit it now. For as long as there is a Voat, PV will be here.
